line: See what is true. Accept what is true. Fix what is false. Do not waste your life defending your pride.
brief: Chad calmly inspects a visibly damaged mechanical assembly on a workbench, accepts the failed part without drama, removes it, and installs the correct replacement while an unused trophy and mirror sit ignored in the background.

line: So making intelligence abundant can create a second scarcity: attention and judgment about what all that intelligence produces.
brief: A large automated workshop rapidly produces many finished mechanisms onto a broad conveyor, but only a narrow inspection station with one calm human operator can carefully judge which few should proceed; abundance upstream meets scarce attention at the decision point.

line: That little separation creates room to think.
brief: Chad stands at a spacious workbench where two physically separated trays keep measured facts apart from social trophies and mirrors, leaving a clear open working area in the middle where he can calmly inspect and decide what to do next.
